```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Load required packages
library(tidyverse)
library(jsonlite)
library(stringr)

agent_colors <- c(
  "A" = rgb(225, 25, 25, maxColorValue = 255),      # red
  "B" = rgb(156, 39, 176, maxColorValue = 255),     # purple
  "C" = rgb(61, 180, 64, maxColorValue = 255)       # green
)

```

## Data Loading and Processing

```{r load}
# READY TO TEST

data_dir <- "../userstudy_logs"

tlx_survey_dir <- "C:/Users/Ryan/PycharmProjects/maisr/userstudy_logs"

preference_dir <- "C:/Users/Ryan/PycharmProjects/maisr/userstudy_logs"

exclude_subjects <- c(17, 9)

################################################################################


# Find all JSON files under session_data folders
json_files <- list.files(
  path = data_dir,
  pattern = "\\.json$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  recursive = TRUE
) %>%
  str_subset("session_data/") # Only keep files under 'session_data'

# Read all files into one dataframe
all_data <- map_dfr(json_files, function(file) {
  json <- fromJSON(file)
  as_tibble(json$episodes)
}) %>%
  filter(!(subject_id %in% exclude_subjects))
head(all_data)


summary_data <- all_data %>%
  group_by(subject_id) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_episode_timesteps = mean(total_timesteps, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_final_targets = mean(final_targets_identified, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_final_threats = mean(final_threats_identified, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
#summary_data


agent_summary <- all_data %>%
  filter(agent_type %in% c("A", "B", "C")) %>%
  group_by(subject_id, agent_type) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_timesteps = mean(total_timesteps, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_targets = mean(final_targets_identified, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_threats = mean(final_threats_identified, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = agent_type,
    values_from = c(avg_timesteps, avg_targets, avg_threats),
    names_glue = "agent{agent_type}_{.value}"
  )
#agent_summary


final_dataset <- summary_data %>%
  left_join(agent_summary, by = "subject_id")
final_dataset

```

### Per-round
```{r agent_level_performance}

# Create dataset with agent and level breakdown
agent_level_data <- all_data %>%
  filter(agent_type %in% c("A", "B", "C")) %>%
  mutate(
    agent_letter = agent_type,
    level_num = level
  ) %>%
  group_by(subject_id, agent_letter, level_num) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_timesteps = mean(total_timesteps, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_targets = mean(final_targets_identified, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_threats = mean(final_threats_identified, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate summary statistics for error bars
agent_level_summary <- agent_level_data %>%
  group_by(agent_letter, level_num) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_timesteps = mean(avg_timesteps, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_timesteps = sd(avg_timesteps, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    #mean_targets = mean(avg_targets, na.rm = TRUE),
    #se_targets = sd(avg_targets, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    mean_threats = mean(avg_threats, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_threats = sd(avg_threats, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Reshape for plotting (combine mean and SE correctly)
plot_summary <- agent_level_summary %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(mean_timesteps, mean_threats), # mean_targets
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "mean_value",
    names_prefix = "mean_"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    agent_level_summary %>%
      pivot_longer(
        cols = c(se_timesteps, se_threats), # se_targets
        names_to = "metric",
        values_to = "se_value",
        names_prefix = "se_"
      ),
    by = c("agent_letter", "level_num", "metric")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = case_when(
      metric == "timesteps" ~ "Mission Duration (steps)",
      #metric == "targets" ~ "Targets Identified",
      metric == "threats" ~ "Threats Identified"
    ),
    agent_label = agent_letter,           # Use A/B/C directly for x-axis
    level_label = paste("Level", level_num)
  )

# Create bar charts for each level
levels_to_plot <- c(1, 3, 5, 7) # 4 removed


for (level in levels_to_plot) {
  level_data <- plot_summary %>% filter(level_num == level)

  p <- ggplot(level_data, aes(x = agent_label, y = mean_value, fill = agent_label)) +
    geom_col(alpha = 0.7, width = 0.6) +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(ymin = mean_value - se_value, ymax = mean_value + se_value),
      width = 0.2, color = "black"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Performance Metrics by Agent - Level", level),
      x = "Agent",
      y = "Mean Value",
      caption = "Error bars represent standard error"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=17),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    axis.line.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
    axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "gray80"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 15, color='black'),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18),
    legend.position = 'None',
    legend.text = element_text(size = 15),
    legend.title = element_blank()) +
    # theme(
    #   legend.position = "none",
    #   axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    #   strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold")
    # ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = agent_colors)

  print(p)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Workload Surveys
```{r tlx_load}
# Load all survey files from subdirectories
survey_files <- list.files(
  tlx_survey_dir,
  pattern = "^tlx_survey_responses_subject_.*\\.json$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  recursive = TRUE
)

# Read and combine all survey responses
survey_data <- map_dfr(survey_files, function(file) {
  subject_id <- str_extract(basename(file), "\\d+")
  
  json_data <- fromJSON(file)
  
  # Ensure it's a data frame/tibble
  df <- as_tibble(json_data)
  
  df %>%
    mutate(subject_id = as.integer(subject_id))
})

# Check column names
print(names(survey_data))

# Pivot to wide format: one row per subject
tlx_wide <- survey_data %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = subject_id,
    names_from = episode_config,  # assuming JSON has this field
    values_from = c(mental_demand, temporal_demand, effort, performance, frustration),
    names_glue = "{episode_config}_{.value}"
  )

head(tlx_wide)


################## Plot ##################

# 1. Add composite workload to long format
tlx_long <- survey_data %>%
  select(subject_id, episode_config, agent, level,
         mental_demand, temporal_demand, effort, performance, frustration, composite_workload) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(mental_demand, temporal_demand, effort, performance, frustration, composite_workload),
    names_to = "component",
    values_to = "score"
  )

# 2. Set factor order so composite is first
tlx_long$component <- factor(
  tlx_long$component,
  levels = c("composite_workload", "mental_demand", "temporal_demand", 
             "effort", "performance", "frustration")
)

tlx_long$component <- factor(
  tlx_long$component,
  levels = c("composite_workload", "mental_demand", "temporal_demand", 
             "effort", "performance", "frustration"),
  labels = c("Composite", "Mental Demand", "Temporal Demand", 
             "Effort", "Performance", "Frustration")
)

# 3. Compute summary stats for plotting
tlx_summary <- tlx_long %>%
  group_by(agent, component) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_score = sd(score, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 4. Faceted plot with composite first
ptlx <- ggplot(tlx_summary, aes(x = agent, y = mean_score, fill = agent)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_score - se_score, ymax = mean_score + se_score),
                width = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ component, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = agent_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 6)) + 
  labs(
    title = "TLX Workload Scores Per Agent",
    x = "Agent",
    y = "Score"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + 
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),   # <-- centers the title
  )

ggsave("outputs/workloadfacet.png",
       plot = ptlx,
       width = dev.size()[1],      # Use current width
       height = dev.size()[2],    # Use current height
       dpi = 300,                  # High resolution
       bg = "white")
```

## Preference Survey heatmap
``` {r preference-load}

# Load teammate survey JSON files
teammate_files <- list.files(
  path = preference_dir,
  pattern = "^teammate_survey_subject_.*\\.json$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  recursive = TRUE
)

get_color_mapping <- function(subject_id) {
  if (subject_id < 24) {
    return(c("red" = "A", "purple" = "B", "green" = "C"))
  } else if (subject_id >= 24 & subject_id <= 32) {
    return(c("green" = "A", "red" = "B", "purple" = "C"))
  } else {
    # Default mapping for subjects > 32 (you can adjust this as needed)
    return(c("red" = "A", "purple" = "B", "green" = "C"))
  }
}

# Combine all survey responses
teammate_data <- map_dfr(teammate_files, function(file) {
  subject_id <- str_extract(basename(file), "\\d+")
  subject_id_num <- as.integer(subject_id)
  
  # Get the appropriate color mapping for this subject
  color_to_agent <- get_color_mapping(subject_id_num)
  
  json <- fromJSON(file)
  as_tibble(json) %>%
    mutate(subject_id = subject_id_num) %>%
    # Map colors to agents using subject-specific mapping
    mutate(
      compared_agents = map(compared_agents, ~ color_to_agent[.x]),
      agent1 = map_chr(compared_agents, 1),
      agent2 = map_chr(compared_agents, 2),
      preferred_overall = color_to_agent[preferred_overall],
      performed_better = color_to_agent[performed_better],
      adapted_better = color_to_agent[adapted_better]
    )
}) %>%
  select(subject_id, episode_config, agent1, agent2,
         preferred_overall, performed_better, adapted_better)

# ------------------------
# Compute mean preference scores for each metric
# ------------------------
metrics <- c("preferred_overall", "performed_better", "adapted_better")

pref_long <- teammate_data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(metrics), names_to = "metric", values_to = "preferred_agent") %>%
  mutate(
    score = ifelse(preferred_agent == agent1, 1,
                   ifelse(preferred_agent == agent2, -1, 0))
  )

# Prepare all agent combinations
agent_levels <- c("A", "B", "C")
pairs <- expand.grid(agent1 = agent_levels, agent2 = agent_levels, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Compute mean scores for each metric
pref_matrix <- pref_long %>%
  group_by(metric, agent1, agent2) %>%
  summarise(mean_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  right_join(
    expand.grid(metric = metrics, agent1 = agent_levels, agent2 = agent_levels),
    by = c("metric", "agent1", "agent2")
  ) %>%
  replace_na(list(mean_score = 0)) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = recode(metric,
                    preferred_overall = "Overall",
                    performed_better = "Searching",
                    adapted_better = "Coordinating")
  )

# ------------------------
# Faceted heatmap plot
# ------------------------
p <- ggplot(pref_matrix, aes(x = agent2, y = agent1, fill = mean_score)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(mean_score, 2)), color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "brown", mid = "white", high = "blue", midpoint = 0,
    name = "Preference for \nrow agent vs. \ncolumn agent"
  ) +
  labs(
    #title = "Teammate Preference Matrices",
    x = "Column Agent",
    y = "Row Agent"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, ncol = 3) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + 
  theme(
    panel.spacing.x = unit(1, "cm"),  # horizontal spacing
    panel.spacing.y = unit(1, "cm"),   # vertical spacing
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),   # <-- centers the title
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),   # <-- smaller title
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11),  # <-- axis title
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 11)
)
p

# Save with the same aspect ratio as what you see on screen
ggsave("outputs/preference_matrices.png",
       plot = p,
       width = dev.size()[1],      # Use current width
       height = dev.size()[2],    # Use current height
       dpi = 300,                  # High resolution
       bg = "white")


```

## Statistical Tests
### Performance
```{r stat}


library(broom)   # for tidy ANOVA results

# 1. ----- Mission Performance Elements vs Agent Type -----

# Convert final_dataset to long format for the three metrics
performance_long <- final_dataset %>%
  select(subject_id,
         agentA_avg_timesteps, agentB_avg_timesteps, agentC_avg_timesteps,
         agentA_avg_targets, agentB_avg_targets, agentC_avg_targets,
         agentA_avg_threats, agentB_avg_threats, agentC_avg_threats) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -subject_id,
    names_to = c("agent", "metric"),
    names_pattern = "agent([ABC])_avg_(.*)"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = case_when(
      metric == "timesteps" ~ "Mission Duration",
      metric == "targets" ~ "Targets Identified",
      metric == "threats" ~ "Threats Identified"
    ),
    agent = factor(agent, levels = c("A", "B", "C"))
  )

# Run separate one-way ANOVA for each metric
anova_results <- performance_long %>%
  group_by(metric) %>%
  do({
    tidy(aov(value ~ agent, data = .)) %>%
      filter(term != "Residuals")    # remove residual rows
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

print("=== Mission Performance ANOVA Results ===")
print(anova_results)


# 2. ----- Composite Workload vs Agent Type -----

# Compute composite workload per subject/agent
composite_workload <- survey_data %>%
  mutate(
    composite_workload = mental_demand + temporal_demand + effort + frustration,
    agent = factor(agent, levels = c("A", "B", "C"))
  )

# Run ANOVA for composite workload
workload_anova <- aov(composite_workload ~ agent, data = composite_workload)
print("=== Composite Workload ANOVA Result ===")
print(summary(workload_anova))

# Optional: Tukey post-hoc test if ANOVA is significant
tukey_workload <- TukeyHSD(workload_anova)
print("=== Tukey Post-hoc for Composite Workload ===")
print(tukey_workload)



```
